introduction.text: In this lesson, you will learn important vocabulary related to the workplace and career in German. You will also practice using these terms in sentences and dialogues.
introduction.culturalNote: In Germany, the concept of 'Berufsausbildung' (vocational training) is highly regarded, and many young people choose to pursue apprenticeships in various fields.

vocabulary.definition: A job or occupation that someone is trained for.
vocabulary.tip: Remember that 'Beruf' is masculine (der), and its plural is 'die Berufe'.

vocabulary.definition: A formal request to be considered for a job.

exampleSentence.translation: I am currently writing my application.

vocabulary.tip: 'Bewerbung' is feminine (die) and its plural form is 'die Bewerbungen'.

vocabulary.definition: A meeting to discuss a job opportunity.

exampleSentence.translation: I have a job interview tomorrow.

vocabulary.tip: This word is neuter (das) and does not change in plural: 'die Vorstellungsgespräche'.

vocabulary.definition: The progression of a person's work life.

exampleSentence.original: Ich plane meine Karriere im Marketing.
exampleSentence.translation: I am planning my career in marketing.

vocabulary.tip: 'Karriere' is feminine (die) and its plural is 'die Karrieren', although it's often used in the singular.

vocabulary.definition: A person who works with you.

exampleSentence.original: Mein Kollege hilft mir bei der Arbeit.
exampleSentence.translation: My colleague helps me with the work.

vocabulary.tip: 'Kollege' is masculine (der) and its plural is 'die Kollegen'.

vocabulary.definition: A job position or role within a company.

exampleSentence.original: Ich habe die Stelle als Lehrer bekommen.
exampleSentence.translation: I got the position as a teacher.

vocabulary.tip: 'Stelle' is feminine (die) and its plural is 'die Stellen'.

grammar.title: Using Subordinate Clauses
grammar.explanation: In German, subordinate clauses can be introduced with 'dass' (that), 'weil' (because), and 'wenn' (if). These clauses provide additional information about the main clause. The verb is placed at the end of the subordinate clause.

rows: Ich gehe, wenn ich Zeit habe.

examples.original: Ich hoffe, dass ich die Stelle bekomme.
examples.translation: I hope that I get the position.
examples.breakdown: Main clause: Ich hoffe (I hope) + subordinate clause: dass ich die Stelle bekomme (that I get the position).

commonMistakes: Confusing word order in subordinate clauses - remember the verb goes to the end.
Using 'weil' incorrectly - make sure to use it to explain reasons.

dialogue.title: Job Interview Conversation
dialogue.context: This conversation takes place during a job interview.

lines.text: Willkommen, Lukas. Können Sie sich bitte vorstellen?
lines.translation: Welcome, Lukas. Can you please introduce yourself?

lines.text: Guten Tag, ich heiße Lukas und habe in der Marketingabteilung gearbeitet.
lines.translation: Good day, my name is Lukas and I have worked in the marketing department.

lines.text: Ich bin kreativ und kann gut im Team arbeiten.
lines.translation: I am creative and can work well in a team.

lines.text: Warum möchten Sie für unser Unternehmen arbeiten?
lines.translation: Why do you want to work for our company?

lines.text: Ich finde Ihre Projekte sehr interessant und möchte meine Karriere hier entwickeln.
lines.translation: I find your projects very interesting and want to develop my career here.

lines.text: Das klingt gut. Haben Sie Fragen?
lines.translation: That sounds good. Do you have any questions?

lines.text: Ja, wie viele Mitarbeiter gibt es in der Marketingabteilung?
lines.translation: Yes, how many employees are there in the marketing department?

culture.title: Work Culture in Germany
culture.text: In Germany, punctuality and professionalism are highly valued in the workplace. Employees are expected to be well-prepared and dedicated to their tasks.
culture.funFact: Many German companies offer extensive training programs for their employees, emphasizing lifelong learning and development.

keyPoints: Learned vocabulary related to work and career.
Engaged in a realistic job interview dialogue.
Gained cultural insights about the workplace in Germany.
summary.nextSteps: Practice using the vocabulary in your own sentences and try to create your own dialogues about job interviews.
